30 Two waves meet.
What is not a necessary condition for the waves to produce a stationary wave?
A
They must be of the same type.
B
They must have the same period.
C
They must have the same wavelength.
D
They must travel in the same direction.

hints: Notice the question asks for what is not necessary, so look for the statement that contradicts how a stationary wave with fixed nodes is made.
Recall that a stationary wave needs two waves with the same frequency, wavelength and type so their superposition stays fixed in place.
Think about the usual example of an incident wave and its reflection from a fixed end and whether those two waves move the same way.
walkthrough: Identify the situation: two waves meet and superpose, and the question tests the conditions for fixed nodes and antinodes of a stationary wave.
State the governing rule: a stationary wave is produced by the superposition of two progressive waves of the same type, same frequency and same wavelength travelling in opposite directions.
Check same type: both waves must produce displacement in the same way so they can add at every point, so option A is a necessary condition.

Check period and wavelength: same period means same frequency, and with the same wave speed $v = f\lambda$ this also means same wavelength, giving a non-moving interference pattern, so options B and C are necessary conditions.

Check direction: if both waves travelled in the same direction at the same speed they would just move together, whereas opposite directions are needed to keep nodes fixed, so same direction is not required.
Therefore travelling in the same direction is the non-necessary condition. This is option D.

A.explanation: Same type is necessary because two waves can only superpose to give fixed nodes if they have the same nature of displacement, for example both transverse on the same string.

B.explanation: Same period is necessary because it means the same frequency $f = 1/T$, so the interference pattern does not drift with time.

C.explanation: Same wavelength $\lambda$ is necessary, linked to same speed and frequency by $v = f\lambda$, so nodes stay at fixed positions.

D.explanation: Travelling in the same direction is not required - a stationary wave is formed by two identical waves travelling in opposite directions.
